description: We’re building a map that helps an astronaut compare Marswalk routes to a science stop. We’ll combine NASA orbital imagery, terrain, and rover observations so explorers can see the trade-offs along each route. Looking for a Universal Event teammate with an interest in GIS, planetary science, or web visualization.
summary: Mars Walk helps an explorer compare routes across real Martian terrain. Choose among nine surveyed areas, set a start and destination, and inspect route grades in 3D alongside rover panoramas and historical infrared imagery. At Enchanted Lake, one 10 m stretch measures 6.1° on a 1 m grid and 3.0° on a 20 m average. Seeing that difference helps a crew decide which parts of a proposed walk need closer inspection.
details:
Mars Walk combines Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE imagery and stereo elevation, Mars Odyssey THEMIS infrared, and rover observations from Perseverance, Curiosity, Spirit and Opportunity. Nine surveys cover Jezero, Gale, Gusev and Meridiani Planum. The globe supports regional elevation profiles from the 200 m USGS HRSC/MOLA grid.

At Enchanted Lake, the 1 m grid flags 100–114 m of the direct route at a 5° study limit. Across the 102–112 m subwindow, the native and averaged grades are 6.065° and 3.016°. The suggested detour adds about 1.9 m of walking and reduces flagged length from 14 m to 0 m. A 2 m lateral shift brings back 10 m. Users can reproduce the decision with the linked map, chart and 3D view. Custom routes check both terrain grids along every segment.

Victoria compares two planned transects within the measured crater wall. Its Cape Verde panorama records a nearby rover viewpoint. Endeavour Rim, Bagnold Dunes and Vera Rubin Ridge connect mapped terrain with documented rover observations. The 100 m THEMIS layer presents historical infrared context. Orbital grade is a planning measurement and footing requires ground assessment.

The team built the app in JavaScript and CesiumJS and used Python and Rasterio to process data. OpenAI Codex assisted with code, data preparation, verification and writing. The fictional astronaut artwork uses ImageGen and is visibly labeled. NASA rover models are credited separately. The earlier Gale portfolio supplied its audited terrain crop, route definitions and Shaler panorama. The Sources links list the data products, software and licenses.
